observed_title: Maxima of asymptotically Gaussian random fields and moderate deviation approximations to boundary crossing probabilities of sums of random variables with multidimensional indices
version: Annals of Probability 34(1), 2006, pp. 80–121; DOI 10.1214/009117905000000378; arXiv:math/0412428v2; 43 PDF pages

read_ranges.scope: entire article: basic conditions, Gaussian and non-Gaussian theorems, multidimensional sums/LIL, empirical-process and scan-statistic applications, proofs, discussion and references

topic_relevance.K01: direct: Sections 2 and 5 establish local and global maxima asymptotics for Gaussian and asymptotically Gaussian fields, with moderate-deviation marginal tails, conditional local-clump limits and cross-cube anti-clustering assumptions.
topic_relevance.K02: adjacent: the proof explicitly modifies the classical double-sum method, and it derives a local Pickands-type constant H(t); its framework is broader than the stationary Gaussian Pickands–Piterbarg setting.
topic_relevance.H01: adjacent: marginal moderate-deviation approximation is a required input (A1)/(B1), but the paper does not prove a general triangular-array Cramér expansion independent of its field applications.
topic_relevance.K04: adjacent: Section 4 applies the framework to maxima of multivariate empirical processes under a smooth positive-density condition.

definitions.name: local correlation scale and tangent field
definitions.statement: For local covariance 1−(1+o(1))||u||^alpha L(||u||)r_t(u/||u||), 0<alpha<=2, define Delta_c by Delta_c^alpha L(Delta_c)=(2c^2)^(-1). The conditional local limit field W_t has mean −||u||^alpha r_t(u/||u||)/2 and covariance [q_t(u)+q_t(v)−q_t(u−v)]/2, q_t(u)=||u||^alpha r_t(u/||u||). Its clump functional is H_K(t)=integral_0^infinity e^y P{sup_{u in [0,K]^d}W_t(u)>y}dy and H(t)=lim_{K→infinity}K^(−d)H_K(t).

definitions.name: asymptotically Gaussian assumptions (C), (A1)–(A5)
definitions.statement: (C) is a uniform local covariance expansion at scale Delta_c. (A1) is a uniform standard-normal moderate-deviation approximation to P{X_c(t)>c−y/c} for bounded positive y. (A2) is weak convergence of the finite-dimensional conditional local increment field given X_c(t)=c−y/c to W_t. (A3) controls an isolated high local increment when the anchor is much below level c; (A4) controls a local-cube exceedance with a low anchor and supplies a uniform Na(γ) error with an endpoint integral condition; (A5) bounds joint high values at separated rescaled locations by ψ(c−γ/c) f(||u||), with f having stretched-exponential decay.

definitions.name: local versus global crossing
definitions.statement: The paper treats a local exceedance on a small cube as a building block, then sums over larger tiles only after a cross-tile joint-exceedance estimate makes the overlaps negligible; this local crossing density is not asserted to be a first-exit density.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.1 (Gaussian field maximum)
assumptions: X is a zero-mean, unit-variance Gaussian field on a neighborhood [D]_delta of bounded Jordan-measurable D.
The local covariance has form (2.7) for 0<alpha<=2, continuous directional r_t, with convergence uniform in t and direction and sup_t,v r_t(v)<infinity.
H(t) is the clump constant defined from the tangent Gaussian field W_t.
theorem_cards.statement: For a large level c, P{sup_{t in D}X(t)>c} is asymptotic to ψ(c) Delta_c^(−d) integral_D H(t)dt, where ψ(c)=(2πc²)^(−1/2)e^(−c²/2). The associated local-block formula (2.8) is uniform over t for blocks of side ell_c Delta_c with ell_c→infinity and ell_c=o(Delta_c^(−1)).
proof_steps: Treat X as the family X_c=X, so (C) holds by (2.7); use the normal tail expansion for (A1).
Conditioning a Gaussian field on X(t)=c−y/c gives explicit conditional means and covariances; expand them at scale Delta_c to get (A2) and the field W_t.
Use Gaussian tail estimates and the local covariance bound to prove (A3) and the separated-pair condition (A5).
Control local-cube exceedances away from a high anchor by a dyadic/Fernique chaining argument, proving (A4).
Apply Theorem 2.5 and Corollary 2.6 to pass from one local block to a bounded Jordan domain.
gaps: Gaussianity supplies conditional normal formulas in this proof; the non-Gaussian theorem needs separate proofs of (A1)–(A5).
The clump constant H(t) is a limit functional, not generally an explicit closed form; explicit evaluation is available only for special tangent fields such as Example 2.2/Lemma 2.3.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems 2.4–2.5 and Corollary 2.6 (asymptotically Gaussian field maxima)
assumptions: X_c is centered and unit variance on [D]_delta and satisfies uniform local covariance condition (C), marginal tail approximation (A1), conditional local field convergence (A2), low-anchor controls (A3),(A4), and separated-pair bound (A5).
Theorem 2.4 uses (C),(A1)–(A4) for a fixed K local cube. Theorem 2.5 additionally uses (A5), with ell_c→infinity and ell_c=o(Delta_c^(−1)).
Corollary 2.6 requires D bounded and Jordan measurable.
theorem_cards.statement: Theorem 2.4 gives P{sup_{u in I_{t,K Delta_c}}X_c(u)>c}~ψ(c)[1+H_K(t)] uniformly in t. Theorem 2.5 gives P{sup_{u in I_{t,ell_c Delta_c}}X_c(u)>c}~ell_c^d ψ(c)H(t) and shows a joint exceedance in this tile and a bounded-volume exterior set is o(ell_c^d ψ(c)). Corollary 2.6 then yields P{sup_{t in D}X_c(t)>c}~ψ(c)Delta_c^(−d) integral_D H(t)dt.
proof_steps: Discretize a fixed small cube using a mesh a Delta_c; (A2) and (A1) give the limiting finite-grid exceedance probability by conditioning on the anchor's distance below c.
Use (A3) to discard anchors far below the threshold and (A4) to bound the error between the grid and continuous cube; then let mesh a decrease to obtain H_K(t) and Theorem 2.4.
Use (A5) with a stretched-exponential pair bound and (A4) for local boundary errors to prove Lemma 5.3: cross-cube joint exceedance is at most s_K K^d ψ(c), with s_K→0.

Cover a large cube by K Delta_c tiles. Theorem 2.4 supplies local tile probabilities and Lemma 5.3 controls overlap; uniform equicontinuity makes K^(−d)H_K(t) uniformly Cauchy, defining H(t) and proving Theorem 2.5.
Tile D at side ell_c Delta_c, use its Jordan boundary to show boundary tiles have negligible volume, and sum local probabilities as a Riemann sum to obtain Corollary 2.6.
gaps: (A1)–(A5) are substantive and uniform hypotheses; a functional CLT or finite-dimensional weak convergence alone does not imply the high-level tail asymptotic.
The paper's asymptotically Gaussian condition (A2) is initially finite-dimensional; the local oscillation controls (A3),(A4) are separately needed for continuous-block suprema.
The limiting formula is a leading asymptotic and gives no finite-c threshold error rate in general.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.8 (moving boundary crossing)
assumptions: Use (C) and moving-boundary counterparts (B1)–(B5), uniformly over t and levels in the boundary range.
Boundary mesh has Delta_bc=o(zeta_c), zeta_c→0, with the boundary-tile contribution condition (2.14).
Within each tile, squared boundary oscillation is o(1) as in (2.18), so ψ(b_c(t)) is stable at the relative scale required.
theorem_cards.statement: The probability that X_c(t)>b_c(t) somewhere in D_c is asymptotic to the integral over D_c of ψ(b_c(t)) Delta_{b_c(t)}^(−d)H(t)dt, under the displayed boundary and cross-tile conditions.
proof_steps: Apply the large local-block approximation at the local boundary minimum to get each tile contribution.
Use the moving-boundary version of the separated-tile bound to show simultaneous exceedances across distinct tiles are negligible.
Squeeze the global event between a sum of tile events and that sum minus cross-tile intersections; the mesh/boundary assumptions turn the sum into the stated integral.
gaps: The boundary must vary slowly enough on the local cube: (2.16),(2.18) are not cosmetic. The result does not cover arbitrary rough or rapidly oscillating thresholds.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.1 (multivariate empirical-process maximum application)
assumptions: Y_i are iid d-dimensional vectors; F is continuously differentiable with each partial derivative positive.
The threshold c→infinity and c=o(n_c^(1/6)); domain is transformed to a bounded Jordan set using t↦F(t).
The paper verifies (C),(B1)–(B5) for the standardized empirical field, including its conditional local increments.
theorem_cards.statement: The one-sided supremum of the standardized multivariate empirical process has the explicit asymptotic (8c²)^(d−1)e^(−2c²) times an integral over the median level set M={t:F(t)=1/2}; the two-sided absolute supremum has twice that leading term. In d=1 the one-sided result reduces to e^(−2c²); in the independent-coordinate d=2 example the constant is (4 log 2)c²e^(−2c²).
proof_steps: Standardize by tau(t)=sqrt(F(t)(1−F(t))) so the field has unit variance; expand its covariance locally to obtain alpha=1 and Delta_c=(2c²)^(−1).
Use the moderate deviation range c=o(n_c^(1/6)) for (B1); condition on the empirical count at t and use binomial increments plus a functional CLT for (B2).
Verify (B3),(B5) by analogues of the multidimensional-sum bounds and large-deviation estimates; modify the local chaining argument to establish (B4).
Compute H(t) from the directional gradient of F and apply the moving-boundary Corollary 2.9 along the median manifold; let the domain trim parameter decrease to zero.
gaps: The c=o(n_c^(1/6)) moderate-deviation range and smooth positive partial derivatives are explicit restrictions.
This is a specialized empirical-process derivation; it does not automatically give anti-concentration bounds for arbitrary empirical maxima.

constant_dependence.explicit: For local covariance exponent alpha and slowly varying L, Delta_c solves Delta_c^alpha L(Delta_c)=(2c²)^(−1). For the standard Brownian increment field in Example 2.2, alpha=1, Delta_c=(2c²)^(−1), H(t)=2^(−4)(t₂−t₁)^(−2), yielding ψ(c)(c^4/4)[a(a₁^(−1)−a₂^(−1))−log(a₂/a₁)]. For the empirical-process application with independent coordinates in d=2, the leading constant is (4 log 2)c²e^(−2c²).
constant_dependence.dependence: The local scaling depends on alpha,L; H(t) depends on the conditional tangent field's drift/covariance. The global domain enters through integral_D H(t)dt. For empirical processes the sample-size condition c=o(n_c^(1/6)) is essential to the cited moderate-deviation approximation.

endpoint_limits.rare_event_input: The marginal tail approximation at level c−y/c must be uniform over t and bounded y; ordinary weak convergence at fixed levels does not control this rare-event scale.
endpoint_limits.clump_input: The conditional local-field limit alone does not control a continuous supremum; (A3),(A4) rule out remote high points within a block.
endpoint_limits.global_additivity: Cross-block joint exceedances must be negligible by (A5) or the moving-boundary analogue. Without it, summing local probabilities double-counts clusters.
endpoint_limits.geometry: The bounded-domain theorem assumes Jordan measurability. Growing domains require explicit boundary-tile negligibility such as (2.14).
endpoint_limits.boundary: Moving thresholds require the local oscillation condition (2.18); the formula is not valid for an arbitrary boundary field.
endpoint_limits.explicit_constants: The clump constant H is positive/finite under the paper's assumptions but generally implicit. Closed-form H appears only for special tangent fields.

reusable_methods.method: Two-stage high-excursion analysis: local conditional clump limit, then global tile summation
reusable_methods.transfer: For a center-cube maximal-operator field indexed by Q(x,r), one would need to derive (i) a uniform marginal moderate-deviation tail at each cube, (ii) the conditional local process as center/radius changes near a high cube, (iii) local oscillation controls and (iv) separated-cube joint bounds. The paper supplies no such field for M_c; this is a migration framework, not an established maximal-operator theorem.

reusable_methods.method: Directional local covariance captures anisotropic index geometry
reusable_methods.transfer: For center and radius coordinates, compute the full local covariance form rather than forcing isotropic distance; the center and scale directions can have different coefficients and possibly different local exponents. The continuity and boundedness hypotheses on r_t must be proved on the selected cube domain.

reusable_methods.method: Boundary crossing density integrated over a level manifold
reusable_methods.transfer: If a center-cube threshold depends on position/scale, check slow boundary variation at the local mesh, then integrate the derived local crossing density. Theorem 2.8 requires (B1)–(B5), boundary tile control and (2.18); it does not license arbitrary threshold optimization.

unchecked: The entire extracted article, including all proofs and references (43 pages), was read. The global tile asymptotic formulas on PDF page 8 were visually checked against a PyMuPDF render.

I checked the logical roles of (A1)–(A5), the dependency of Theorem 2.5 on the cross-tile lemma, and the domain/threshold restrictions stated in the empirical-process application. I did not independently reprove every Berry–Esseen, Fernique, moderate-deviation or strong-approximation result cited by the authors.

Author results are separated from the proposed center-cube maximal-operator transfer. The latter remains an inference whose required cube-indexed tail, local covariance, oscillation and anti-clustering conditions are not established by this paper.
